title: Семейный разговор в кабинете  (Family Talk in the Office)

segments.t: Chef Viktor Barinov proudly shows his daughter Katya around his new office at the Italian restaurant Arcobaleno. Katya casually asks her father to hire her, sparking a prickly family argument about why neither of them stayed in touch over the past year.
Я тебя и дольше не видела.
У меня всегда были свои причины.
Шеф, там картошку и помидоры привезли.
Let's examine the tense father-daughter conversation between Chef Barinov and Katya.
'Here are my new apartments.' In everyday Russian, 'new' flows straight into 'apartments' without extra linking words.
'It is very cozy here in your place.' Katya uses an affectionate diminutive adverb to tease her father about the decor.
'Previously this office belonged to a woman.' Notice how Russian puts 'earlier' and 'womanly' together in a short, direct phrase where word endings show how the ideas connect.
'I see you have already settled in.' Here Katya anchors the thought on 'watch, look' and finishes on 'to settled', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
'Of course, tell me how your life is.' In everyday Russian, 'of course, certainly' flows straight into 'life' without extra linking words.
'I am currently looking for a new job.' Katya pairs 'right now' with 'work' directly, since spoken Russian skips English filler words like 'the', 'a', and 'is'.
'Dad, will you hire me to work with you?' In spoken Russian, the words stay in their normal statement order and Katya's rising voice at the end turns the line into a question.
'You did not call for a whole year!' Here Chef Barinov anchors the thought on 'year' and finishes on 'called', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
Я тебя и дольше не видела.
'I have gone even longer without seeing you.' In everyday Russian, 'without' flows straight into 'saw' without extra linking words.
У меня всегда были свои причины.
'I always had my own reasons.' Russians say 'by me' or 'with us' where English says 'I have' or 'we have', without needing a separate word for 'have'.
Шеф, там картошку и помидоры привезли.
'Chef, they delivered potatoes and tomatoes there.' Lyova interrupts with an impersonal plural past verb reporting a kitchen delivery.
'Do you not see that I am busy right now!' Here Chef Barinov anchors the thought on 'see' and finishes on 'busy', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.

'All right, Dad, I am leaving already.' Katya announces her departure in the first-person singular present tense. Now listen to the entire office scene between Chef Barinov, Katya, and Lyova without interruption.

Offended that her father prioritizes potatoes and tomatoes over their conversation, Katya walks out on him. Next, we see where Katya goes to look for work instead. Until next time!
